For a home equity line, send the current home-equity-line pamphlet instead; always record date, method, and recipient.

heading: § 1024.7 Good faith estimate.
text: (d) Content and form of GFE. The GFE form is set out in appendix C to this part. The loan originator must prepare the GFE in accordance with the requirements of this section and the Instructions in appendix C to this part. The instructions in appendix C to this part allow for flexibility in the preparation and distribution of the GFE in hard copy and electronic format.
clause: When a customer applies for a home loan, the loan officer handling that application must fill out our standard cost-estimate sheet exactly as the official template and its line-by-line directions require, so every charge and term appears in the right place. The officer may complete and hand over the estimate on paper or send it electronically, such as by email, whichever suits the customer. The officer then keeps a copy of what was provided in the customer's file.

heading: § 1024.7 Good faith estimate.
text: (e) Tolerances for amounts included on GFE. (1) Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section, the actual charges at settlement may not exceed the amounts included on the GFE for: (i) The origination charge; (ii) While the borrower's interest rate is locked, the credit or charge for the interest rate chosen; (iii) While the borrower's interest rate is locked, the adjusted origination charge; and (iv) Transfer taxes. (2) Except as provided in paragraph (f) of this section, the sum of the charges at settlement for the following services may not be greater than 10 percent above the sum of the amounts included on the GFE: (i) Lender-required settlement services, where the lender selects the third party settlement service provider; (ii) Lender-required services, title services and required title insurance, and owner's title insurance, when the borrower uses a settlement service provider identified by the loan originator; and (iii) Government recording charges. (3) The amounts charged for all other settlement services included on the GFE may change at settlement.
clause: For each quoted home loan, the closing team compares the final bill to the quote and saves the check in the account. During any rate hold, the final amount cannot top the quote for our loan-making fee, any rate credit or fee, the adjusted loan-making fee, or transfer taxes. For required closing help we pick, required help and title work and coverage from a company we named, and government filing fees, the combined total may be at most 10 percent over the combined quote; other quoted closing services may change.

heading: § 1024.7 Good faith estimate.
text: (g) GFE is not a loan commitment. Nothing in this section shall be interpreted to require a loan originator to make a loan to a particular borrower. The loan originator is not required to provide a GFE if the loan originator does not have available a loan for which the borrower is eligible.
clause: Sending an early cost worksheet never promises approval or funding, and a home-loan advisor may turn down any customer. If we have no home loan the customer qualifies for, do not send the worksheet. Keep a file note showing which options were checked and why none fit.

heading: § 1024.8 Use of HUD-1 or HUD-1A settlement statements.
text: (c) Violations of section 4 of RESPA (12 U.S.C. 2603). A violation of any of the requirements of this section will be deemed to be a violation of section 4 of RESPA. An inadvertent or technical error in completing the HUD-1 or HUD-1A shall not be deemed a violation of section 4 of RESPA if a revised HUD-1 or HUD-1A is provided in accordance with the requirements of this section within 30 calendar days after settlement.
clause: When a closer finds a small accidental or clerical mistake on a customer’s final home-loan cost sheet, the closer must correct that sheet and send the corrected sheet to the customer within 30 calendar days after the closing date. Do this for every home purchase or refinance file where we issued that cost sheet, even if the customer has not complained. The closer must keep the first sheet, the corrected sheet, proof of the send date, and a short note about the mistake in the loan file.

heading: § 1030.11 Additional disclosure requirements for overdraft services.
text: (c) Disclosure of account balances. If an institution discloses balance information to a consumer through an automated system, the balance may not include additional amounts that the institution may provide to cover an item when there are insufficient or unavailable funds in the consumer's account, whether under a service provided in its discretion, a service subject to Regulation Z (12 CFR part 1026), or a service to transfer funds from another account of the consumer. The institution may, at its option, disclose additional account balances that include such additional amounts, if the institution prominently state s that any such balance includes such additional amounts and, if applicable, that additional amounts are not available for all transactions.
clause: For every customer account, staff who maintain self-serve phone, ATM, online, or app screens must make the main available amount leave out extra dollars we might use to pay a purchase or withdrawal when the account is short or money is on hold, including case-by-case coverage, credit-plan coverage, or moves from the customer’s other account. If we show a second amount with those extra dollars, the screen or message must say clearly beside it that it includes them and, when true, that they cannot be used for every transaction.

heading: § 1030.3 General disclosure requirements.
text: (a) Form. Depository institutions shall make the disclosures required by §§ 1030.4 through 1030.6 of this part, as applicable, clearly and conspicuously, in writing, and in a form the consumer may keep. The disclosures required by this part may be provided to the consumer in electronic form, subject to compliance with the consumer consent and other applicable provisions of the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (E-Sign Act) (15 U.S.C. 7001 et seq.). The disclosures required by §§ 1030.4(a)(2) and 1030.8 may be provided to the consumer in electronic form without regard to the consumer consent or other provisions of the E-Sign Act in the circumstances set forth in those sections. Disclosures for each account offered by an institution may be presented separately or combined with disclosures for the institution's other accounts, as long as it is clear which disclosures are applicable to the consumer's account.
clause: For every deposit account, Deposit Operations puts the opening facts, later account updates, and statement details on paper or in a message the customer can save or print, with key points easy to spot. Send them by email or online only after the customer’s electronic-delivery OK is recorded, except a customer’s request for account details and product promotions may go by email or online without that OK only in the cases those product rules allow. If several accounts share one packet, mark which details fit the customer’s account.

heading: § 1030.3 General disclosure requirements.
text: (b) General. The disclosures shall reflect the terms of the legal obligation of the account agreement between the consumer and the depository institution. Disclosures may be made in languages other than English, provided the disclosures are available in English upon request.
clause: When the account team writes or updates any paperwork that describes what a deposit account pays, charges, or requires, every detail must match the deal the customer actually signed, nothing more and nothing less. Staff may give customers this paperwork in Spanish or another language if that serves them better. Whenever a customer asks for it in English, the branch must hand over the English version, so each branch keeps an English copy on hand.

heading: § 1030.3 General disclosure requirements.
text: (c) Relation to Regulation E (12 CFR Part 1005). Disclosures required by and provided in accordance with the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq.) and its implementing Regulation E (12 CFR Part 1005) that are also required by this part may be substituted for the disclosures required by this part.
clause: Some accounts come with an information sheet we must give about electronic money movement, such as card or online transfers. When that sheet already covers the account details we must give the customer, the account-opening team may use that one sheet for both purposes instead of preparing a separate account-information sheet. The team notes in the account file which sheet the customer received and keeps a copy.

heading: § 1030.3 General disclosure requirements.
text: (e) Oral response to inquiries. In an oral response to a consumer's inquiry about interest rates payable on its accounts, the depository institution shall state the annual percentage yield. The interest rate may be stated in addition to the annual percentage yield. No other rate may be stated.
clause: When a customer calls or stops in and asks what any of our accounts earns, the team member who answers must quote the account's yearly yield percentage, the figure that already builds in compounding. That person may also mention the plain underlying rate it is based on, but must not quote any other rate. This applies to every account we offer.

heading: § 1030.5 Subsequent disclosures.
text: (a) Change in terms—(1) Advance notice required. A depository institution shall give advance notice to affected consumers of any change in a term required to be disclosed under § 1030.4(b) of this part if the change may reduce the annual percentage yield or adversely affect the consumer. The notice shall include the effective date of the change. The notice shall be mailed or delivered at least 30 calendar days before the effective date of the change. (2) No notice required. No notice under this section is required for: (i) Variable-rate changes. Changes in the interest rate and corresponding changes in the annual percentage yield in variable-rate accounts. (ii) Check printing fees. Changes in fees assessed for check printing. (iii) Short-term time accounts. Changes in any term for time accounts with maturities of one month or less.
clause: Before we change any price or rule on a deposit account sheet, the product owner lists each customer who could earn less than the quoted yearly yield or be worse off. Deposit operations sends by mail or hands over a letter stating the start day at least 30 calendar days earlier, and keeps a copy with the send date in the account file. Skip this for rate moves on changeable-rate accounts and the matching yield move, fees for printing checks, or fixed-length savings ending one month or less after opening.

heading: § 1030.6 Periodic statement disclosures.
text: (b) Special rule for average daily balance method. In making the disclosures described in paragraph (a) of this section, institutions that use the average daily balance method and that calculate interest for a period other than the statement period shall calculate and disclose the annual percentage yield earned and amount of interest earned based on that period rather than the statement period. The information in paragraph (a)(4) of this section shall be stated for that period as well as for the statement period.
clause: For savings accounts where we work out earnings by averaging each day's balance and we figure those earnings over a stretch of time different from the span covered by the customer's regular account summary, the statements team must base the yearly earnings rate and the dollar amount earned on that earnings stretch, not the summary span. Every time the team prepares and sends a summary, it must also give the length of the earnings stretch as well as the length of the summary span.

heading: § 1030.7 Payment of interest.
text: (c) Date interest begins to accrue. Interest shall begin to accrue not later than the business day specified for interest-bearing accounts in section 606 of the Expedited Funds Availability Act (12 U.S.C. 4005) and in § 229.14 of that act's implementing Regulation CC (12 CFR part 229). Interest shall accrue until the day funds are withdrawn.
clause: For each customer account that pays earnings, Deposit Operations starts counting earnings no later than the business day our availability schedule sets for that deposit. The team keeps counting through the day the customer takes the money out. Deposit Operations records the start and stop dates in the account history.

heading: § 1030.8 Advertising.
text: (a) Misleading or inaccurate advertisements. An advertisement shall not: (1) Be misleading or inaccurate or misrepresent a depository institution's deposit contract; or (2) Refer to or describe an account as “free” or “no cost” (or contain a similar term) if any maintenance or activity fee may be imposed on the account. The word “profit” shall not be used in referring to interest paid on an account.
clause: Before any public sales piece runs, the Marketing reviewer matches each statement about checking, savings, or CDs against the current rate sheet, charge list, and customer agreement, and blocks anything untrue or different. If a monthly upkeep or transaction charge can ever apply, the piece must not say the product costs nothing, has no charge, or use like wording; for amounts we credit on balances, say earnings or yield, never 'profit.' The reviewer initials and dates the approval and files the final piece with the papers used.

heading: § 1030.8 Advertising.
text: (c) When additional disclosures are required. Except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section, if the annual percentage yield is stated in an advertisement, the advertisement shall state the following information, to the extent applicable, clearly and conspicuously: (1) Variable rates. For variable-rate accounts, a statement that the rate may change after the account is opened. (2) Time annual percentage yield is offered. The period of time the annual percentage yield will be offered, or a statement that the annual percentage yield is accurate as of a specified date. (3) Minimum balance. The minimum balance required to obtain the advertised annual percentage yield. For tiered-rate accounts, the minimum balance required for each tier shall be stated in close proximity and with equal prominence to the applicable annual percentage yield. (4) Minimum opening deposit. The minimum deposit required to open the account, if it is greater than the minimum balance necessary to obtain the advertised annual percentage yield. (5) Effect of fees. A statement that fees could reduce the earnings on the account. (6) Features of time accounts. For time accounts: (i) Time requirements. The term of the account. (ii) Early withdrawal penalties: A statement that a penalty will or may be imposed for early withdrawal. (iii) Required interest payouts. For noncompounding time accounts with a stated maturity greater than one year that do not compound interest on an annual or more frequent basis, that require interest payouts at least annually, and that disclose an APY determined in accordance with section E of appendix A of this part, a statement that interest cannot remain on deposit and that payout of interest is mandatory.
clause: Before Marketing runs any ad quoting a yearly savings yield, add applicable points plainly; keep the final ad and checklist. Say if the rate can change after the customer starts; how long the yield lasts or its as-of date; least money for that yield, each balance level beside its yield as strongly; any higher starting amount; charges can cut earnings. For fixed-length savings add length; early take-out will/may bring a charge; over one year without yearly adding-back but required yearly payout, earnings must be paid out, not left in.

heading: § 1030.8 Advertising.
text: (d) Bonuses. Except as provided in paragraph (e) of this section, if a bonus is stated in an advertisement, the advertisement shall state the following information, to the extent applicable, clearly and conspicuously: (1) The “annual percentage yield,” using that term; (2) The time requirement to obtain the bonus; (3) The minimum balance required to obtain the bonus; (4) The minimum balance required to open the account, if it is greater than the minimum balance necessary to obtain the bonus; and (5) When the bonus will be provided.
clause: Before any promo for a savings, checking, or certificate product mentions extra money for opening it or keeping money in it, the marketing owner makes the piece easy to spot and read and adds, when they apply: the exact words "annual percentage yield" by the rate; how long the customer must qualify; the least money needed to earn it; the least money needed to open it, if that is higher; and when we credit it. A compliance reviewer checks five points, initials the final piece, and files it before release.

heading: § 1030.8 Advertising.
text: (e) Exemption for certain advertisements—(1) Certain media. If an advertisement is made through one of the following media, it need not contain the information in paragraphs (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(4), (c)(5), (c)(6)(ii), (d)(4), and (d)(5) of this section: (i) Broadcast or electronic media, such as television or radio; (ii) Outdoor media, such as billboards; or (iii) Telephone response machines. (2) Indoor signs. (i) Signs inside the premises of a depository institution (or the premises of a deposit broker) are not subject to paragraphs (b), (c), (d) or (e)(1) of this section. (ii) If a sign exempt by paragraph (e)(2) of this section states a rate of return, it shall: (A) State the rate as an “annual percentage yield,” using that term or the term “APY.” The sign shall not state any other rate, except that the interest rate may be stated in conjunction with the annual percentage yield to which it relates. (B) Contain a statement advising consumers to contact an employee for further information about applicable fees and terms.
clause: For TV, radio, similar aired spots, outdoor boards such as billboards, and recorded phone-answer lines, do not require Marketing to add the change-after-opening, offer-period, larger opening-deposit, fees-reduce-earnings, early-withdrawal-penalty, or bonus opening-balance/payment-timing lines. Do not apply the account-promotion content rules to signs inside our branches or a broker’s office that places deposits with us. If such an indoor sign shows a yield, it must say 'annual percentage yield' or 'APY', show no other yield except the related interest rate, and tell customers to ask an employee about fees and terms.

heading: § 312.11 Safe harbor programs.
text: (b) Criteria for approval of self-regulatory program guidelines. Proposed safe harbor programs must demonstrate that they meet the following performance standards: (1) Program requirements that ensure operators subject to the self-regulatory program guidelines (“subject operators”) provide substantially the same or greater protections for children as those contained in §§ 312.2 through 312.8, and 312.10. (2) An effective, mandatory mechanism for the independent assessment of subject operators' compliance with the self-regulatory program guidelines. At a minimum, this mechanism must include a comprehensive review by the safe harbor program, to be conducted not less than annually, of each subject operator's information privacy and security policies, practices, and representations. The assessment mechanism required under this paragraph can be provided by an independent enforcement program, such as a seal program. (3) Disciplinary actions for subject operators' non-compliance with self-regulatory program guidelines. This performance standard may be satisfied by: (i) Mandatory, public reporting of any action taken against subject operators by the industry group issuing the self-regulatory guidelines; (ii) Consumer redress; (iii) Voluntary payments to the United States Treasury in connection with an industry-directed program for violators of the self-regulatory guidelines; (iv) Referral to the Commission of operators who engage in a pattern or practice of violating the self-regulatory guidelines; or (v) Any other equally effective action.
clause: Our policy team writes the trade group's membership rules, which must protect kids' personal information at least as strongly as the standard rules everyone else follows. At least once a year, our audit staff or an outside trust-badge group fully checks each member company's privacy and security policies, actual practices, and public claims. If a member breaks the rules, we publicly announce any action we take, make things right for affected customers, require voluntary payments to the United States Treasury, or report repeat offenders to the government.

heading: § 312.11 Safe harbor programs.
text: (e) Post-approval modifications to self-regulatory program guidelines. Approved safe harbor programs must submit proposed changes to their guidelines for review and approval by the Commission in the manner required for initial approval of guidelines under paragraph (c)(2) of this section. The statement required under paragraph (c)(4) of this section must describe how the proposed changes affect existing provisions of the guidelines.
clause: If we run an oversight program that a federal office has signed off on, and we later want to change any of its written rules, our program manager must send the planned changes to that office and wait for its okay before using them, following the same steps as the original sign-off. The package must include a written summary explaining how each planned change would alter the rules already in place. The manager keeps the okay letter on file.

heading: § 312.11 Safe harbor programs.
text: (h) Operators' participation in a safe harbor program. An operator will be deemed to be in compliance with the requirements of §§ 312.2 through 312.8, and 312.10 if that operator complies with Commission-approved safe harbor program guidelines. In considering whether to initiate an investigation or bring an enforcement action against a subject operator for violations of this part, the Commission will take into account the history of the subject operator's participation in the safe harbor program, whether the subject operator has taken action to remedy such non-compliance, and whether the operator's non-compliance resulted in any one of the disciplinary actions set forth in paragraph (b)(3) of this section.
clause: Privacy Operations must keep our company enrolled and in good standing in the approved outside privacy plan for covered online accounts, following its rules so items 312.2 through 312.8, and 312.10 are treated as met. When staff find a gap, they fix it fast, write down what happened, the fix, the date, and any penalty tied to b(3), and keep proof of plan membership and history. When Legal weighs a review or case, Privacy Operations sends that full history and fix record.

heading: § 312.12 Voluntary Commission approval processes.
text: (a) Parental consent methods. An interested party may file a written request for Commission approval of parental consent methods not currently enumerated in § 312.5(b). To be considered for approval, a party must provide a detailed description of the proposed parental consent methods, together with an analysis of how the methods meet § 312.5(b)(1). The request shall be filed with the Commission's Office of the Secretary. The Commission will publish in the Federal Register a document seeking public comment on the request. The Commission shall issue a written determination within 120 days of the filing of the request.
clause: If a product team wants a new way to get a parent's okay that is not on our allowed list, the Privacy Officer sends the federal reviewers a letter describing the approach in full and explaining point by point why it works as well as the listed options. The package goes to the reviewers' intake office; the Privacy Officer logs the send date and watches for the public post inviting comments. The reviewers answer in writing within 120 days, and the Privacy Officer keeps that answer on file.

heading: § 312.12 Voluntary Commission approval processes.
text: (b) Support for the internal operations of the website or online service. An interested party may file a written request for Commission approval of additional activities to be included within the definition of support for the internal operations of the website or online service. To be considered for approval, a party must provide a detailed justification why such activities should be deemed support for the internal operations of the website or online service, and an analysis of their potential effects on children's online privacy. The request shall be filed with the Commission's Office of the Secretary. The Commission will publish in the Federal Register a document seeking public comment on the request. The Commission shall issue a written determination within 120 days of the filing of the request.
clause: If we want a new behind-the-scenes use of a customer site or app that may reach kids accepted as needed to run it, the Privacy Lead sends a signed letter to the federal records desk that takes these kids' data letters. The letter must explain in detail why that use belongs there and review how it could affect those kids. The Privacy Lead keeps the letter, proof it arrived, any posting asking for outside views, and the answer, due within 120 days after arrival.

heading: § 312.4 Notice.
text: (a) General principles of notice. It shall be the obligation of the operator to provide notice and obtain verifiable parental consent prior to collecting, using, or disclosing personal information from children. Such notice must be clearly and understandably written, complete, and must contain no unrelated, confusing, or contradictory materials.
clause: Before we ask for, work with, or pass along any details about a kid, the account-opening agent must send the parent a short plain letter that says all we want, why, and who gets it, and nothing extra or mixed in. The agent must get the parent’s clear yes in a way we can check, and save the letter and yes with the account before any data entry begins.

heading: § 312.4 Notice.
text: (b) Direct notice to the parent. An operator must make reasonable efforts, taking into account available technology, to ensure that a parent of a child receives direct notice of the operator's practices with regard to the collection, use, or disclosure of personal information from children, including notice of any material change in the collection, use, or disclosure practices to which the parent has previously consented.
clause: Our sign-up team must try hard, with the tools we have, to make sure a kid's mom or dad gets a message straight from us explaining what details we gather from kids, how we work with those details, and who we share them with. If we later make a big change to any of that after the mom or dad already said yes, the team sends them a fresh message describing the change. Record when each message went out and to whom.

heading: § 312.5 Parental consent.
text: (a) General requirements. (1) An operator is required to obtain verifiable parental consent before any collection, use, or disclosure of personal information from children, including consent to any material change in the collection, use, or disclosure practices to which the parent has previously consented. (2) An operator must give the parent the option to consent to the collection and use of the child's personal information without consenting to disclosure of his or her personal information to third parties, unless such disclosure is integral to the website or online service. An operator required to give the parent this option must obtain separate verifiable parental consent to such disclosure.
clause: For each kid account, before we gather, use, or pass along a kid's details, staff must get and file a checkable okay from the adult in charge; do it again before any big change to what that adult already approved. The sign-up must let that adult say yes to our gathering and using those details while saying no to passing them to outside companies, unless passing them is needed to run the site or app. If outside sharing is not needed to run it, get a separate checkable okay first.

heading: § 312.6 Right of parent to review personal information provided by a child.
text: (a) Upon request of a parent whose child has provided personal information to a website or online service, the operator of that website or online service is required to provide to that parent the following: (1) A description of the specific types or categories of personal information collected from children by the operator, such as name, address, telephone number, email address, hobbies, and extracurricular activities; (2) The opportunity at any time to refuse to permit the operator's further use or future online collection of personal information from that child, and to direct the operator to delete the child's personal information; and (3) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a means of reviewing any personal information collected from the child. The means employed by the operator to carry out this provision must: (i) Ensure that the requestor is a parent of that child, taking into account available technology; and (ii) Not be unduly burdensome to the parent.
clause: When a mom or dad asks about details their kid gave us on our site or app, customer care first confirms the asker is that kid's mom or dad with our checking tools, keeping it easy for them. Then send a letter listing the kinds of details we gather from kids, like name, address, phone, email, hobbies, and activities, and show what we hold on that kid. Give them a way, usable anytime, to stop more gathering or use and to have the kid's details removed; log each ask.

heading: § 312.6 Right of parent to review personal information provided by a child.
text: (b) Neither an operator nor the operator's agent shall be held liable under any Federal or State law for any disclosure made in good faith and following reasonable procedures in responding to a request for disclosure of personal information under this section.
clause: When a parent asks to see or get details we hold about their child, the account-care teammate checks identity and our approval steps before sharing anything. Share only what the teammate honestly believes should be shared for that parent, and record the ask, the checks done, and what was sent. If those steps were followed honestly, our company and anyone working for us are not responsible under U.S. or state rules for that sharing.

heading: § 312.6 Right of parent to review personal information provided by a child.
text: (c) Subject to the limitations set forth in § 312.7, an operator may terminate any service provided to a child whose parent has refused, under paragraph (a)(2) of this section, to permit the operator's further use or collection of personal information from his or her child or has directed the operator to delete the child's personal information.
clause: When a kid's mom or dad tells us they no longer agree to our gathering or working with the kid's details going forward, or asks us to erase those details, the account team may close the kid's account or shut off any feature we give the kid. Before closing anything, the team checks our data-handling limits to confirm the closure is allowed. The team then records the adult's request, the date, and the closure in the account file, and sends the adult a letter confirming the account is closed.

heading: § 312.8 Confidentiality, security, and integrity of personal information collected from children.
text: (c) Before allowing other operators, service providers, or third parties to collect or maintain personal information from children on the operator's behalf, or before releasing children's personal information to such entities, the operator must take reasonable steps to determine that such entities are capable of maintaining the confidentiality, security, and integrity of the information and must obtain written assurances that such entities will employ reasonable measures to maintain the confidentiality, security, and integrity of the information.
clause: Before any outside company gathers or holds kids' details for us, or before we send those details over, the vendor owner must look into whether the company can keep them private, safe, and accurate. The vendor owner must get a signed promise that the company will use sensible safeguards, then file the check and promise with the account record.

heading: § 314.3 Standards for safeguarding customer information.
text: (a) Information security program. You shall develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive information security program that is written in one or more readily accessible parts and contains administrative, technical, and physical safeguards that are appropriate to your size and complexity, the nature and scope of your activities, and the sensitivity of any customer information at issue. The information security program shall include the elements set forth in § 314.4 and shall be reasonably designed to achieve the objectives of this part, as set forth in paragraph (b) of this section.
clause: The operations owner must keep one or more data-safety documents staff can open fast for every customer and account, with people rules, computer controls, and building/paper protections fitting our size, tangle, work, and how private details are. Before collecting or using customer details, and whenever size, work, systems, sites, or privacy level changes, the owner must use and update them, name one lead, list likely dangers, check outside companies touching details, set update steps, and aim to block likely dangers and unapproved use causing real harm or hassle.

heading: § 314.3 Standards for safeguarding customer information.
text: (b) Objectives. The objectives of section 501(b) of the Act, and of this part, are to: (1) Insure the security and confidentiality of customer information; (2) Protect against any anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information; and (3) Protect against unauthorized access to or use of such information that could result in substantial harm or inconvenience to any customer.
clause: Every employee must keep each customer's personal and account details private and accurate, and never share them with anyone who has no business need. Team leads must watch for anything that could expose or corrupt our files—like phishing emails, lost laptops, or weak passwords—and fix or report it the same day. The IT team must block anyone who is not approved from viewing or using customer details, and log every incident where details might have leaked, because a leak could cause a customer serious trouble or loss.

heading: § 314.4 Elements.
text: (a) Designate a qualified individual responsible for overseeing and implementing your information security program and enforcing your information security program (for purposes of this part, “Qualified Individual”). The Qualified Individual may be employed by you, an affiliate, or a service provider. To the extent the requirement in this paragraph (a) is met using a service provider or an affiliate, you shall: (1) Retain responsibility for compliance with this part; (2) Designate a senior member of your personnel responsible for direction and oversight of the Qualified Individual; and (3) Require the service provider or affiliate to maintain an information security program that protects you in accordance with the requirements of this part.
clause: Name one person with the right skills to put in place, run, and make sure staff follow our safeguards for customer information. This person may work for us, a sister company, or an outside vendor. If a sister company or outside vendor fills the role, we still own the duty to follow these rules, name one of our senior managers to guide and check that person's work, and make the sister company or vendor keep safeguards in place that keep us safe as required.

heading: § 314.4 Elements.
text: (b) Base your information security program on a risk assessment that identifies reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of customer information that could result in the unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction, or other compromise of such information, and assesses the sufficiency of any safeguards in place to control these risks. (1) The risk assessment shall be written and shall include: (i) Criteria for the evaluation and categorization of identified security risks or threats you face; (ii) Criteria for the assessment of the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of your information systems and customer information, including the adequacy of the existing controls in the context of the identified risks or threats you face; and (iii) Requirements describing how identified risks will be mitigated or accepted based on the risk assessment and how the information security program will address the risks. (2) You shall periodically perform additional risk assessments that reexamine the reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of customer information that could result in the unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction, or other compromise of such information, and reassess the sufficiency of any safeguards in place to control these risks.
clause: Our technology lead keeps a written review of how customer details could realistically be leaked, stolen, changed, or destroyed by anyone inside or outside the company, and whether our current protections are strong enough. It must state the standards for sorting and rating each problem, for judging how well our systems keep customer details private, accurate, and accessible, and for deciding which problems we fix and which we accept. The technology lead repeats this review on a regular schedule.

heading: § 314.4 Elements.
text: (d)(1) Regularly test or otherwise monitor the effectiveness of the safeguards' key controls, systems, and procedures, including those to detect actual and attempted attacks on, or intrusions into, information systems. (2) For information systems, the monitoring and testing shall include continuous monitoring or periodic penetration testing and vulnerability assessments. Absent effective continuous monitoring or other systems to detect, on an ongoing basis, changes in information systems that may create vulnerabilities, you shall conduct: (i) Annual penetration testing of your information systems determined each given year based on relevant identified risks in accordance with the risk assessment; and (ii) Vulnerability assessments, including any systemic scans or reviews of information systems reasonably designed to identify publicly known security vulnerabilities in your information systems based on the risk assessment, at least every six months; and whenever there are material changes to your operations or business arrangements; and whenever there are circumstances you know or have reason to know may have a material impact on your information security program.
clause: Our IT safety lead must prove protections for customer account and card data work, including catching real or tried break-ins. For computers, keep always-on watching or scheduled break-in drills and weak-spot checks; lacking working always-on watching or ongoing change-spotting, run an annual drill from that year's risk list and check publicly known weak spots at least every six months, after major changes in how we work or who we work with, and when events we know or should know could seriously hurt protections. Record the check, result, fix, and date.

heading: § 314.4 Elements.
text: (e) Implement policies and procedures to ensure that personnel are able to enact your information security program by: (1) Providing your personnel with security awareness training that is updated as necessary to reflect risks identified by the risk assessment; (2) Utilizing qualified information security personnel employed by you or an affiliate or service provider sufficient to manage your information security risks and to perform or oversee the information security program; (3) Providing information security personnel with security updates and training sufficient to address relevant security risks; and (4) Verifying that key information security personnel take steps to maintain current knowledge of changing information security threats and countermeasures.
clause: Our Security Office trains every employee on protecting customer data at hiring and at least once a year, refreshing the material whenever our risk reviews uncover new dangers. We keep enough skilled security specialists on staff, through an affiliate, or through an outside firm to run and supervise our data-protection work. Those specialists get regular bulletins and classes matched to current risks, and the Security Office checks each quarter that senior staff keep up with new scams and defenses, recording each check.

heading: § 314.4 Elements.
text: (f) Oversee service providers, by: (1) Taking reasonable steps to select and retain service providers that are capable of maintaining appropriate safeguards for the customer information at issue; (2) Requiring your service providers by contract to implement and maintain such safeguards; and (3) Periodically assessing your service providers based on the risk they present and the continued adequacy of their safeguards.
clause: The Vendor Management team watches over every outside company that stores, sends, or otherwise touches customers' personal details. Before we hire one, the team checks that it can protect that data well, and we only sign on companies that pass. Each written agreement must make the company promise to put strong data protections in place and keep them working. On a regular schedule, the team re-checks each company, more often when a leak there would do more harm, and writes down whether the protections still hold up.

heading: § 314.4 Elements.
text: (g) Evaluate and adjust your information security program in light of the results of the testing and monitoring required by paragraph (d) of this section; any material changes to your operations or business arrangements; the results of risk assessments performed under paragraph (b)(2) of this section; or any other circumstances that you know or have reason to know may have a material impact on your information security program.
clause: Our security lead must look over and update our plan for keeping customer data safe whenever: our system checks and ongoing watch produce findings; we make a big shift in how we run the business or in outside companies we work with; we finish a review of what could go wrong with customer data; or we learn, or should have learned, of something else that could seriously weaken that protection. The security lead writes down what changed and why, and tells staff whose daily work is affected.

heading: § 314.4 Elements.
text: (h) Establish a written incident response plan designed to promptly respond to, and recover from, any security event materially affecting the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer information in your control. Such incident response plan shall address the following areas: (1) The goals of the incident response plan; (2) The internal processes for responding to a security event; (3) The definition of clear roles, responsibilities, and levels of decision-making authority; (4) External and internal communications and information sharing; (5) Identification of requirements for the remediation of any identified weaknesses in information systems and associated controls; (6) Documentation and reporting regarding security events and related incident response activities; and (7) The evaluation and revision as necessary of the incident response plan following a security event.
clause: Our Data Safety Manager keeps a written playbook for quick action and recovery after any hack, outage, or leak that could really harm customers’ details we hold; it covers every customer whose details are in our care. The playbook states its aims, step-by-step actions, named owners, approval levels, how we share updates inside the company and with outside partners, how we fix weak tools and safeguards, and what we write down and send. After each such problem, the manager reviews what happened, updates the playbook as needed, and files notes.

heading: § 681.1 Duties regarding the detection, prevention, and mitigation of identity theft.
text: (c) Periodic Identification of Covered Accounts. Each financial institution or creditor must periodically determine whether it offers or maintains covered accounts. As a part of this determination, a financial institution or creditor must conduct a risk assessment to determine whether it offers or maintains covered accounts described in paragraph (b)(3)(ii) of this section, taking into consideration: (1) The methods it provides to open its accounts; (2) The methods it provides to access its accounts; and (3) Its previous experiences with identity theft.
clause: Once a year, the Compliance Owner lists every customer account we open or keep and flags any where someone pretending to be a customer could plausibly hurt that customer or us. For each flagged account, they complete a 3-point check: how people can join, how they can get in or move money, and what past impersonation cases taught us. They save the dated list, each in-or-out call, and the reasons in the identity-fraud file, and send the in-scope list to Fraud and Product.

heading: § 681.1 Duties regarding the detection, prevention, and mitigation of identity theft.
text: (d) Establishment of an Identity Theft Prevention Program—(1) Program requirement. Each financial institution or creditor that offers or maintains one or more covered accounts must develop and implement a written Identity Theft Prevention Program (Program) that is designed to detect, prevent, and mitigate identity theft in connection with the opening of a covered account or any existing covered account. The Program must be appropriate to the size and complexity of the financial institution or creditor and the nature and scope of its activities. (2) Elements of the Program. The Program must include reasonable policies and procedures to: (i) Identify relevant Red Flags for the covered accounts that the financial institution or creditor offers or maintains, and incorporate those Red Flags into its Program; (ii) Detect Red Flags that have been incorporated into the Program of the financial institution or creditor; (iii) Respond appropriately to any Red Flags that are detected pursuant to paragraph (d)(2)(ii) of this section to prevent and mitigate identity theft; and (iv) Ensure the Program (including the Red Flags determined to be relevant) is updated periodically, to reflect changes in risks to customers and to the safety and soundness of the financial institution or creditor from identity theft.
clause: Our fraud team must keep a written plan, matched to our size and work, for spotting, stopping, and limiting harm when someone opens or uses an account under another person's name. It must list the warning signs that matter for each account we offer or keep open, and staff must watch for them. Anyone who spots one must act at once under the plan to protect the customer and company. Management must refresh the plan and warning signs on a set schedule as risks to customers and our stability change.

heading: § 681.1 Duties regarding the detection, prevention, and mitigation of identity theft.
text: (e) Administration of the Program. Each financial institution or creditor that is required to implement a Program must provide for the continued administration of the Program and must: (1) Obtain approval of the initial written Program from either its board of directors or an appropriate committee of the board of directors; (2) Involve the board of directors, an appropriate committee thereof, or a designated employee at the level of senior management in the oversight, development, implementation and administration of the Program; (3) Train staff, as necessary, to effectively implement the Program; and (4) Exercise appropriate and effective oversight of service provider arrangements.
clause: Operations keeps one written playbook for spotting and stopping misuse of a customer’s name, card, home loan, or account, and keeps it working for every customer account. Before first use, our top directors or their chosen director group sign off on that written playbook; Operations files the sign-off with it. A top director, that group, or one named senior manager must own setting it up, updating it, running it, checking outside companies that handle customer accounts, and teaching staff as needed to do it, with completion recorded.

heading: § 681.2 Duties of card issuers regarding changes of address.
text: (b) Definitions. For purposes of this section: (1) Cardholder means a consumer who has been issued a credit or debit card. (2) Clear and conspicuous means reasonably understandable and designed to call attention to the nature and significance of the information presented.
clause: These rules cover every customer we have given a credit card or a debit card. Wherever our procedures call for a message that must stand out, the team writing it, usually customer communications, must use plain wording an ordinary reader can grasp and a layout (headline, bold type, position on the page) that draws the eye to what the message says and why it matters. The communications lead reviews each template against both points before first use and keeps a signed note of that check.

heading: § 681.2 Duties of card issuers regarding changes of address.
text: (d) Alternative timing of address validation. A card issuer may satisfy the requirements of paragraph (c) of this section if it validates an address pursuant to the methods in paragraph (c)(1) or (c)(2) of this section when it receives an address change notification, before it receives a request for an additional or replacement card.
clause: For any card account, when a customer gives a different mailing address, the card service teammate confirms it at that time: send the customer an address-update confirmation with a fast way to report wrong details, or use another approved account check. The teammate writes the check used and the result in the account before anyone asks for another card on that account. If that confirmation is finished first, treat the later card request as already covered for the address check.

heading: § 1020.220 Customer identification program requirements for banks.
text: (b) Exemptions. The appropriate Federal functional regulator, with the concurrence of the Secretary, may, by order or regulation, exempt any bank or type of account from the requirements of this section. The Federal functional regulator and the Secretary shall consider whether the exemption is consistent with the purposes of the Bank Secrecy Act and with safe and sound banking, and may consider other appropriate factors. The Secretary will make these determinations for any bank or type of account that is not subject to the authority of a Federal functional regulator.
clause: Our Compliance Officer may ask our main federal supervisor to excuse the whole company, or one type of account, from the identity checks we run at opening; it counts only if the supervisor issues a written decision and the government's chief finance official agrees. Before seeking it, the Compliance Officer records why it would not weaken our defenses against dirty money or our financial health. If we have no federal supervisor, the chief finance official decides alone. Keep the approval on file and apply it only to the accounts named.

heading: § 1020.220 Customer identification program requirements for banks.
text: (c) Other requirements unaffected. Nothing in this section relieves a bank of its obligation to comply with any other provision in this chapter, including provisions concerning information that must be obtained, verified, or maintained in connection with any account or transaction.
clause: Finishing the identity check for a new customer never cancels the other information duties we have. For every account and everything a customer does with us, the employee opening or handling the account must still collect, confirm, and keep on file any other details the company is required to have. If one detail serves two purposes, record it once and note where it is kept. Supervisors spot-check files each month to make sure nothing was skipped.

heading: § 1020.315 Transactions of exempt persons.
text: (a) General. No bank is required to file a report otherwise required by § 1010.311 with respect to any transaction in currency between an exempt person and such bank, or, to the extent provided in paragraph (e)(6) of this section, between such exempt person and other banks affiliated with such bank. (A limitation on the exemption described in this paragraph (a) is set forth in paragraph (f) of this section.)
clause: When a customer is on our approved cash-handling list, tellers must not send the large-cash form for cash moving between that customer and us. The same applies to cash moving between that customer and another company in our corporate group only when the list shows that company is covered for that customer. Before skipping the form, read the list notes; if a note ends this treatment for that customer or that cash activity, send the form as usual.

heading: § 1020.315 Transactions of exempt persons.
text: (d) Annual review. At least once each year, a bank must review the eligibility of an exempt person described in paragraphs (b)(4) to (7) of this section to determine whether such person remains eligible for an exemption. As part of its annual review, a bank must review the application of the monitoring system required to be maintained by paragraph (h)(2) of this section to each existing account of an exempt person described in paragraphs (b)(6) or (b)(7) of this section.
clause: At least once each year, the account-servicing lead checks every customer marked in cash-report waiver groups four through seven, confirms the customer still qualifies, and records the date, result, and proof in the customer file. In that same yearly check, the compliance operations analyst tests how the required cash-activity watchlist is used on every open account of customers in groups six or seven, and saves the sample and findings.

heading: § 1020.315 Transactions of exempt persons.
text: (f) Limitation on exemption. A transaction carried out by an exempt person as an agent for another person who is the beneficial owner of the funds that are the subject of a transaction in currency is not subject to the exemption from reporting contained in paragraph (a) of this section.
clause: For any customer on our no-cash-form list, the teller or banker taking or giving cash must ask whether the customer is only handling that cash for someone else and who the money really belongs to. If another person really owns the money, do not use the list for that cash move: start the same cash form used for everyday customers and send it to Compliance the same day. Record in the account notes the customer's answer, the real owner's name and role, and the form number.

heading: § 1020.320 Reports by banks of suspicious transactions.
text: (c) Exceptions. A bank is not required to file a SAR for a robbery or burglary committed or attempted that is reported to appropriate law enforcement authorities, or for lost, missing, counterfeit, or stolen securities with respect to which the bank files a report pursuant to the reporting requirements of 17 CFR 240.17f-1.
clause: If a branch is robbed or someone tries to rob it, or a person breaks in or tries to break in, the branch manager must call the police at once and Security must save the police case number, date, and office called. For stock or bond certificates that are gone, taken, or fake, Operations must send the separate market form for those certificates and keep the confirmation. With that proof in the account record, the Financial Crime team does not prepare an unusual-activity write-up and notes the reason.

heading: § 1020.320 Reports by banks of suspicious transactions.
text: (e) Confidentiality of SARs. A SAR, and any information that would reveal the existence of a SAR, are confidential and shall not be disclosed except as authorized in this paragraph (e). For purposes of this paragraph (e) only, a SAR shall include any suspicious activity report filed with FinCEN pursuant to any regulation in this chapter. (1) Prohibition on disclosures by banks—(i) General rule. No bank, and no director, officer, employee, or agent of any bank, shall disclose a SAR or any information that would reveal the existence of a SAR. Any bank, and any director, officer, employee, or agent of any bank that is subpoenaed or otherwise requested to disclose a SAR or any information that would reveal the existence of a SAR, shall decline to produce the SAR or such information, citing this section and 31 U.S.C. 5318(g)(2)(A)(i), and shall notify FinCEN of any such request and the response thereto. (ii) Rules of Construction. Provided that no person involved in any reported suspicious transaction is notified that the transaction has been reported, this paragraph (e)(1) shall not be construed as prohibiting: (A) The disclosure by a bank, or any director, officer, employee, or agent of a bank, of: (1) A SAR, or any information that would reveal the existence of a SAR, to FinCEN or any Federal, State, or local law enforcement agency, or any Federal regulatory authority that examines the bank for compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act, or any State regulatory authority administering a State law that requires the bank to comply with the Bank Secrecy Act or otherwise authorizes the State authority to ensure that the bank complies with the Bank Secrecy Act; or (2) The underlying facts, transactions, and documents upon which a SAR is based, including but not limited to, disclosures: (i) To another financial institution, or any director, officer, employee, or agent of a financial institution, for the preparation of a joint SAR; or (ii) In connection with certain employment references or termination notices, to the full extent authorized in 31 U.S.C. 5318(g)(2)(B); or (B) The sharing by a bank, or any director, officer, employee, or agent of the bank, of a SAR, or any information that would reveal the existence of a SAR, within the bank's corporate organizational structure for purposes consistent with Title II of the Bank Secrecy Act as determined by regulation or in guidance. (2) Prohibition on disclosures by government authorities. A Federal, State, local, territorial, or Tribal government authority, or any director, officer, employee, or agent of any of the foregoing, shall not disclose a SAR, or any information that would reveal the existence of a SAR, except as necessary to fulfill official duties consistent with Title II of the Bank Secrecy Act. For purposes of this section, “official duties” shall not include the disclosure of a SAR, or any information that would reveal the existence of a SAR, in response to a request for disclosure of non-public information or a request for use in a private legal proceeding, including a request pursuant to 31 CFR 1.11.

heading: § 1020.320 Reports by banks of suspicious transactions.
text: (f) Limitation on liability. A bank, and any director, officer, employee, or agent of any bank, that makes a voluntary disclosure of any possible violation of law or regulation to a government agency or makes a disclosure pursuant to this section or any other authority, including a disclosure made jointly with another institution, shall be protected from liability to any person for any such disclosure, or for failure to provide notice of such disclosure to any person identified in the disclosure, or both, to the full extent provided by 31 U.S.C. 5318(g)(3).
